Here are the latest release notes for Python 3.12: **Link:** https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html **Key highlights** | Area | New / Changed in 3.12 | |------|------------------------| | **Interpreter** | *Isolated sub‑interpreters* – each sub‑interpreter now has its own GIL and separate state, making it safer to run multiple interpreters in the same process. | | **Error messages** | Much clearer syntax‑error messages (e.g., pinpointing the exact token) and improved tracebacks that show the exact line/column of the problem. | | **Performance** | *Zero‑cost exception handling* improvements, faster function calls, and better startup time. | | **Profiling** | Integrated support for Linux `perf` (via `-X perf`) to profile Python code without external tools. | | **Typing** | New `typing.ParamSpec` features, `typing.Self` for self‑type annotations, and stricter `typing.Final` enforcement. | | **Pattern matching** | Expanded structural pattern matching (PEP 634) with support for mapping patterns that can match any mapping type, not just `dict`. | | **Standard Library** | • `zoneinfo` now supports IANA time‑zone database updates automatically.
• `asyncio` adds `TaskGroup` improvements and better cancellation handling.
• `statistics` gains `multimode` function.
• `pathlib` now accepts `bytes` paths on Windows. | | **Deprecations / Removals** | • The `distutils` package is officially deprecated (will be removed in a future release).
• Several legacy APIs in `collections` and `asyncio` have been removed. | | **Build & CPython internals** | • New *per‑interpreter* GIL state APIs for embedding scenarios.
• Refactored bytecode optimizer for more efficient code generation. | | **Security** | • Updated OpenSSL bindings to 3.0.x series.
• Hardened hash randomization defaults. | **How to read the full notes** The full “What’s New in Python 3.12” document walks through each change in detail, provides example code, and links to the relevant PEPs. You can view it directly at the URL above or in the local Python installation under `Doc/whatsnew/3.12.rst`.
